answer: Each new agent must solve a unique proof-of-work cipher over its own public key. A keypair is free, but a registered identity costs compute plus a locked stake, and neither can be copied to a second key. Minting a thousand puppets means paying that price a thousand times, while an honest agent pays once. This fable turns a cheap swarm into an expensive one. Standing also decays when idle, like a lotus withering without water, so dormant fakes never recover their cost. To win weight an attacker must outspend honest nodes in electricity and capital; the funding wallet is his audit trail.
